## Summary

Keep the preceding measured class during a pointer transform, then measure the edited design when the gesture ends. This is the small class-timing checkpoint after merged #50.

```text
begin transform → retain class
move → edit geometry; retain class and derived GP budget
release → clear retained class and measure edited design
cancel → clear retained class and restore design
```

## Evidence

- **Before:** The new mock regression failed: resizing a Huge Base Bubble displayed Class 4 while the pointer was held and Class 2 was required.
  **After:** Both supplied-SWF and mock flows export changed scale during the hold while class/budget remain stable, increase class on release, and restore prior parts/class with one Undo.
- Formatting, TypeScript, 486 rule tests (6,040 assertions), production build and all four affected browser cases pass (47.5s, no skips).
- ActionScript resize move/release and their bytecode confirm this timing. Correct the backlog documentation: rotation release has no direct class-update call. This editor still remeasures on either transform release, so exact rotation-release behavior remains explicit open fidelity work.
- No media, generated data, persistence schema or saved drag-fix changes.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Revert restores immediate class measurement during pointer transforms.

**Blast Radius:** editor

Class-based readouts, validation and affordability share the retained class until the gesture ends.

input.title: feat: connect authored creator save and exit flow
input.body:
## Summary

Connect the authored save/exit dialog to the live editor.

```text
SAVE → validate / refresh suggestions → name form → persist submission
  failure → error screen, consumed ID persisted
  success → code screen → return to same editor / exit
Exit → confirmation → cancel / leave
```

Keep the editor canvas mounted and inert behind the dialog. Successful game saves replace the avatar and hold pause until Exit; an upgrade is selected only once.

## Evidence

- **Before:** SAVE immediately returned to the previous screen, and Exit left without confirmation.
  **After:** formatting, TypeScript, 519 rule/parser tests (6,299 assertions), production build and all 25 affected native/mock browser cases pass across the broad and continuation runs, without skips.
- The interrupted broad run passed 20 cases before its browser closed; the heavy-avatar case and four remaining palette/help cases then passed in a 1.5-minute continuation. No timeout, retry setting or assertion was weakened.
- New flows verify loaded versus empty fresh names, verbatim whitespace, Cancel, failed-ID persistence through reload, repeated copies, code/copy, return to editing, unavailable sharing and retained canvas identity. Existing enemy-stat, medal, palette validation, code round-trip, edit cancellation, native quality and secondary-help checks remain.
- Native/mock name and code captures were inspected. The unpublished rebase onto merged #73 preserves the complete verified tree.
- Source: `TankCreatorScreen.SaveExitMouseUp/_-VM/_-Ez/_-IS/_-2J/_-Av` and `PlayerProfile.SetNewProfileData`. Profile identity is separate from a submitted author's name; no recent-author preference is invented.
- Naming moves into the authored form; JSON draft Export remains. The modal is a sibling of the inert editor under their common stage. Viewer/details work is separate. Repeated upgrade-editor saves and complete original-playthrough timing remain source-supported behavior awaiting broader runtime comparison.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Reverting restores the prior UI flow. Saved local copies remain compatible; no profile schema or media changes.

**Blast Radius:** creator

Save/exit navigation and game-edit pause/replacement change. Existing rendering owners and the unavailable-service boundary remain intact.

output.body:
## Summary

Connect the authored save/exit dialog to the live editor.

```text
SAVE → validate / refresh suggestions → name form → persist submission
  failure → error screen, consumed ID persisted
  success → code screen → return to same editor / exit
Exit → confirmation → cancel / leave
```

Keep the editor canvas mounted and inert behind the dialog. Successful game saves replace the avatar and hold pause until Exit; an upgrade is selected only once.

## Evidence

- **Before:** SAVE immediately returned to the previous screen, and Exit left without confirmation.
  **After:** formatting, TypeScript, 519 rule/parser tests (6,299 assertions), production build and all 25 affected native/mock browser cases pass across the broad and continuation runs, without skips.
- The interrupted broad run passed 20 cases before its browser closed; the heavy-avatar case and four remaining palette/help cases then passed in a 1.5-minute continuation. No timeout, retry setting or assertion was weakened.
- New flows verify loaded versus empty fresh names, verbatim whitespace, Cancel, failed-ID persistence through reload, repeated copies, code/copy, return to editing, unavailable sharing and retained canvas identity. Existing enemy-stat, medal, palette validation, code round-trip, edit cancellation, native quality and secondary-help checks remain.
- Native/mock name and code captures were inspected. The unpublished rebase onto merged #73 preserves the complete verified tree.
- Source: `TankCreatorScreen.SaveExitMouseUp/_-VM/_-Ez/_-IS/_-2J/_-Av` and `PlayerProfile.SetNewProfileData`. Profile identity is separate from a submitted author's name; no recent-author preference is invented.
- Naming moves into the authored form; JSON draft Export remains. The modal is a sibling of the inert editor under their common stage. Viewer/details work is separate. Repeated upgrade-editor saves and complete original-playthrough timing remain source-supported behavior awaiting broader runtime comparison.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Reverting restores the prior UI flow. Saved local copies remain compatible; no profile schema or media changes.

**Blast Radius:** creator

Save/exit navigation and game-edit pause/replacement change. Existing rendering owners and the unavailable-service boundary remain intact.
